decision: Bind read-only filesystem qualification to the expected effective uid of the dedicated coordinator qrexec service identity and reject root execution.

permission_checks_only.correctness: Insufficient: proves permissions for whichever account executed the check, not necessarily the deployed qrexec service identity.
permission_checks_only.robustness: Can yield misleading evidence if invoked from an unrelated restricted account.
permission_checks_only.regressionRisk: Low but leaves an evidence-binding gap.
permission_checks_only.qa: Existing tests cover write denial but not identity provenance.

username_or_environment_binding.correctness: Weaker: names and environment variables are mutable labels and do not establish kernel execution identity.
username_or_environment_binding.robustness: Susceptible to configuration drift and spoofed environment values.
username_or_environment_binding.qa: Easy to test but weak evidence.

effective_uid_binding.correctness: Strongest minimal option: binds the filesystem capability test to the kernel effective uid used by the service process.
effective_uid_binding.robustness: Fails closed on uid mismatch and root execution while preserving existing file, descriptor, parent-directory and symlink checks.
effective_uid_binding.latency: Negligible; two local identity syscalls and no qrexec round trip.
effective_uid_binding.resourceUse: No daemon, database, watcher or persistent state.
effective_uid_binding.regressionRisk: Small and localized to Phase-1 qualification; deployment must provide expectedServiceUid explicitly.
effective_uid_binding.qa: Adds root and mismatched-uid negative tests plus identity evidence in the report.

whyWinner: It closes the provenance gap with kernel-derived identity, adds essentially zero runtime cost, and does not widen MissionQueue or transport semantics.
failuresAndLessons: A read-only permission result is not sufficient evidence unless it is bound to the actual service execution identity.
Username/environment labels are weaker than kernel effective uid for deployment qualification.
Phase-1 read-only qrexec qualification should never run as root because root can invalidate ordinary discretionary-permission assumptions.
safety: Synthetic/defensive qualification only; no financial transactions, payment data, fraud workflow, or security-control weakening.
